title: Compact-open continuous coinduced cochains and the explicit augmented contraction
statement:
Let $J$ be a compact Hausdorff abelian topological group, written additively, let $k$ be a topological field, and let $V$ be a Hausdorff topological $k$-vector space, with continuous vector operations. Put $R=C(J,V)$ with the compact-open topology and jointly continuous $J$-action $(t\cdot f)(y)=f(y+t)$. Let $B^q(J,R)$ be the continuous homogeneous equivariant cochains and $C^q(J,R)=C(J^q,R)$ the continuous inhomogeneous cochains, with the differentials and cochain isomorphism of [lem-sfb-topological-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates]; all complexes here are complexes of abstract $k$-vector spaces and vanish in negative degrees. Define $D^q=C(J^{q+1},V)$ with differential
$$(\delta\phi)(x_0,\ldots,x_{q+1})=\sum_{i=0}^{q+1}(-1)^i\phi(x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,x_{q+1}).$$
The maps
$$\Theta_q(F)(x_0,\ldots,x_q)=F(x_0,\ldots,x_q)(0),\qquad
\Theta_q^{-1}(\phi)(x_0,\ldots,x_q)(y)=\phi(x_0+y,\ldots,x_q+y)$$
are mutually inverse $k$-linear cochain isomorphisms $B^\bullet(J,R)\simeq D^\bullet$. For $q\geq1$ the formulas
$$(h_q\phi)(x_0,\ldots,x_{q-1})=\phi(0,x_0,\ldots,x_{q-1})$$
define actual continuous cochains. Let $i:V[0]\to D^\bullet$ be the constant inclusion in degree zero and let $p:D^\bullet\to V[0]$ be evaluation at $0$ in degree zero, zero elsewhere. Then $pi=1$ and $\delta h+h\delta=1-ip$, taking $h_0=0$. Hence these formulas and the homogeneous-to-inhomogeneous isomorphism give a chain homotopy equivalence $C^\bullet(J,R)\simeq V[0]$, in particular an isomorphism $Q(C^\bullet(J,R))\simeq Q(V[0])$ in $D(k\text{-Vect})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In every positive degree every closed cochain has a continuous primitive. No discreteness or completeness of $V$ is assumed.

proof.text: Every point of $J$ has the compact neighbourhood $J$ itself. Apply [lem-coef-hausdorff-compact-neighborhood-basis] to obtain the compact neighbourhood basis required by [lem-coef-compact-open-currying]. The latter gives joint evaluation $(f,y)\mapsto f(y)$ on $C(J,V)\times J$ (take $A=C(J,V)$ and $g=1$), and continuous transposition. In particular pointwise addition and scalar multiplication on $R$ are jointly continuous: uncurry them to $(f,g,y)\mapsto f(y)+g(y)$ and $(a,f,y)\mapsto af(y)$, then transpose. Negation is identical. Evaluation at each point is continuous, so distinct functions can be separated using Hausdorffness of $V$; thus $R$ is Hausdorff. Uncurry the proposed action to $(t,f,y)\mapsto f(y+t)$ and transpose to prove its joint continuity. Translations are linear and $(s\cdot(t\cdot f))(y)=f(y+s+t)=((s+t)\cdot f)(y)$; $0$ acts identically. These verifications use continuity of the given vector operations and group addition, with the product topology. This supplies the hypotheses for the coordinate theorem with coefficients $R$.

proof.text: For each $q\geq0$, evaluation at zero composed with a continuous $F:J^{q+1}\to R$ is continuous by step 1. Conversely, for $\phi\in D^q$, the function $(x,y)\mapsto\phi(x_0+y,\ldots,x_q+y)$ is continuous by coordinatewise addition; its transpose into $C(J,V)$ is continuous by [lem-coef-compact-open-currying]. Its value $S_q\phi$ is equivariant, since $(S_q\phi)(x_0+t,\ldots,x_q+t)(y)=\phi(x_0+t+y,\ldots,x_q+t+y)= (t\cdot(S_q\phi)(x_0,\ldots,x_q))(y)$, using commutativity of $J$. Hence both displayed arrows in the statement have the asserted domains. Each is $k$-linear by pointwise operations.

proof.text: Pointwise, $\Theta_qS_q\phi(x)=\phi(x)$. Conversely equivariance gives $(S_q\Theta_qF)(x)(y)=F(x_0+y,\ldots,x_q+y)(0)=(y\cdot F(x))(0)=F(x)(y)$. Thus $S_q=\Theta_q^{-1}$. From the homogeneous differential in [lem-sfb-topological-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates], evaluation commutes with its finite alternating sum, so $\Theta_{q+1}\delta_BF=\delta_D\Theta_qF$. The differential on $D$ has continuous values because each omission map is continuous; its square is zero because omitting positions $a<b$ in either order contributes signs $(-1)^{a+b-1}$ and $(-1)^{a+b}$. This also checks the complex directly. Invertibility of $\Theta$ now makes both arrows cochain maps. In negative degrees use the unique arrows between zero spaces.

proof.text: For $q\geq1$, insertion $J^q\to J^{q+1}$, $x\mapsto(0,x_0,\ldots,x_{q-1})$, is continuous, so precomposition defines the stated linear $h_q:D^q\to D^{q-1}$. The maps $i$ and $p$ are linear and $pi=1$. They are cochain maps: $\delta_D^0(i(v))(x_0,x_1)=v-v=0$, and every other required equation involving $V[0]$ has both sides zero. Take $h_0:D^0\to0$ to be zero. These are arrows of abstract vector spaces; no continuity as operators between cochain spaces is asserted or needed.

proof.text:
For $q\geq1$, at $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_q)$ the two expansions are
$$ (\delta_D^{q-1}h_q\phi)(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{q}(-1)^j\phi(0,x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_j},\ldots,x_q), $$
$$ (h_{q+1}\delta_D^q\phi)(x)=\phi(x)+\sum_{j=0}^{q}(-1)^{j+1}\phi(0,x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_j},\ldots,x_q). $$
The indexed terms cancel in pairs, giving $\delta h+h\delta=1$ in positive degree, where $ip=0$. In degree zero, $(h_1\delta_D^0\phi)(x)=\phi(x)-\phi(0)$, precisely $(1-ip)\phi(x)$. In negative degree all terms vanish. The cancellations remain valid in characteristic two.

proof.text: Let $T=\Theta\Phi^{-1}:C^\bullet(J,R)\to D^\bullet$, using the cochain isomorphism $\Phi:B^\bullet(J,R)\to C^\bullet(J,R)$ of [lem-sfb-topological-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates], whose hypotheses were checked in step 1. Define $I=T^{-1}i$ and $P=pT$. Then $PI=1$, and $H_q=T_{q-1}^{-1}h_qT_q$ satisfies $dH+Hd=T^{-1}(1-ip)T=1-IP$. This is the asserted chain homotopy equivalence with the actual continuous-cochain complex. For a closed $c\in C^q$, $q>0$, the explicit primitive is $T_{q-1}^{-1}h_qT_qc$: the same equality gives $d(H_qc)=c$, and each constituent was proved to have continuous-cochain values.

proof.text: To obtain the derived isomorphism without an additional homotopy-invariance assertion, compute cohomology directly. The positive-degree cancellation in step 5 makes every closed $\phi$ a boundary $\delta h\phi$. In degree zero $\delta\phi=0$ means $\phi(x_1)=\phi(x_0)$ for all $x_0,x_1$; hence $\phi=i(\phi(0))$, and there are no incoming boundaries. Therefore $p:D^\bullet\to V[0]$ induces the inverse of the constant inclusion on $H^0$, and is an isomorphism on zero cohomology in every other degree. So $P=pT$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The localization functor $Q$ in that statement inverts it and yields $Q(C^\bullet(J,R))\simeq Q(V[0])$. Every operation used finite sums, composition, evaluation or insertion; no completeness or discreteness hypothesis on $V$ entered.
